steps.body: The strip is a piece of the number line: its left edge is 0 and its right edge is 1. The column edges mark the tenths.
steps.narration: The strip is a piece of the number line: its left edge is 0 and its right edge is 1. The column edges mark the tenths.

widget.prompt: Shade the strip to show 0.4. Each column is one tenth.

commonCounts.feedback: The count of shaded columns must match the tenths digit of 0.4 — that digit is 4, so 4 columns.

widget.successFeedback: Exactly 4 of the 10 columns — 4 tenths, which the decimal writes as 0.4.
widget.lowFeedback: The shaded amount is still below the target. Each column is one tenth — count the shaded columns against the decimal.
widget.highFeedback: The shaded amount has gone past the target. Each column is one tenth — count the shaded columns against the decimal.

predict.prompt: The strip runs from 0 on the left to 1 on the right. Shading 0.4 fills the strip to a point — where?
predict.reveal: 0.4 is 4 of the 10 steps from 0 to 1 — one step short of halfway. Halfway is 0.5, five steps.

explanationVariants: Each column is one tenth, so 4 columns writes as 0.4.

widget.prompt: A unit square is split into 10 equal columns, and 4 of them are shaded. Write the shaded amount as a decimal.

commonErrors.feedback: That is the count of shaded columns, and a count of parts is a whole number. Each column is one tenth of the square, so 4 columns is 4 tenths, written with the 4 in the tenths place.
That puts the 4 in the hundredths place, which would mean 4 cells of a hundred-cell grid. This square has only 10 columns, so each shaded column is a tenth of the whole.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Each column is one tenth of the square. Count the shaded columns and write that count in the tenths place, directly after the decimal point.

explanationVariants: The 6 sits in the tenths place, so the fraction is 6/10.

widget.prompt: Which fraction names the same amount as 0.6?

options.feedback: Correct — the digit 6 sits in the tenths place, so 0.6 means 6 of 10 equal parts.
A denominator of 100 would mean 6 hundredths, written 0.06. The digit 6 in 0.6 sits one place higher — in the tenths place.
That fraction has the part count and the number of equal pieces swapped. The decimal names 6 pieces out of 10 equal pieces, so 6 belongs on top.
A denominator of 1 would make this 6 whole units. The decimal point in 0.6 says the amount is less than one whole, cut into 10 equal parts.
